papers.title: The Sleep-Wake Classification Performance of Pediatric-Trained Machine Learning Algorithms for Raw Accelerometer Data.
papers.abstract: Actigraphy sleep-wake classification methods increasingly seek to leverage raw acceleration data and machine-learning-based classification, but performance evaluation in pediatrics is limited. We trained machine-learning models using pediatric data and compared their sleep-wake classification performance with existing algorithms for children. Sixty-five children (46% female, ages 5.3-17.7 years) completed in-lab overnight polysomnography and wore a GENEActiv device on their non-dominant wrist. The acceleration data were converted into 30-second epochs and aligned with physician-scored sleep-wake data from electroencephalography. Eight machine-learning models were trained using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Epoch-by-epoch analyses generated performance metrics (e.g., balanced accuracy [BA]) and discrepancy analyses provided overall sleep duration bias estimates. The combination of highest performance and least bias was used to rank using Euclidean distance scores - where a lower score represents closer to perfect performance and zero bias. For benchmarking, we included GGIR sleep scoring algorithms and an adult trained random forest classifier. Overall, 560.1 hours of polysomnography and actigraphy data were collected (74.4% of epochs were scored as sleep). The pediatric-trained local-global long-short term memory (LSTM) classifier had the most optimal epoch-by-epoch performance (e.g., BA=0.85, sensitivity=0.88, specificity=0.83, ROC-AUC=0.95, and Cohen's kappa=0.67). These metrics exceeded that of an adult-trained random forest classifier and GGIR-based algorithms. Discrepancy analyses revealed that overall sleep duration was underestimated by an average of 25 minutes using the LSTM classifier with no proportional bias. We trained eight pediatric sleep-wake classifiers that had a strong ability to detect sleep and wake, with the LSTM classifier being most optimal.

papers.title: Partial lesions of hypocretin neurons of the rat lateral hypothalamus affect wake and sleep regulation under increased sleep pressure
papers.abstract: Hypocretin(orexin)-producing neurons in the lateral hypothalamic area are important for sleep and wake regulation in mammals and their damage in humans manifests clinically as narcolepsy. While in previous studies experimentally induced massive loss of these neurons revealed their physiological importance, small lesions and their manifestations can uncover more subtle features of sleep regulation and help understand the delicate processes in early stages of pathogenesis of narcolepsy. We studied the effects of partial lesions (approximately 30%) of hypocretin producing neurons in the lateral hypothalamus on sleep patterns and EEG in rats. The lesions did not change the normal sleep and wake pattern in undisturbed rats. The effects of lesions manifested under increased sleep pressure after six hours of sleep deprivation, when they led to accelerated dynamics of compensatory slow wave sleep. The lesions also led to a slight decrease in theta frequency in wakefulness and in REM sleep, which we observed during undisturbed sleep and wake behavior as well as after sleep deprivation.

papers.title: Cross-Band Coupling of EEG Infraslow Oscillations during NREM Sleep in Mice.
papers.abstract: The infraslow oscillation (ISO) is a ~ 0.02 Hz rhythmic fluctuation in electroencephalographic (EEG) power during NREM sleep. Prior studies were limited to sigma-band ISO, linked to rhythmic norepinephrine release in mice. Whether ISOs exist in other bands, and how ISOs across bands are coupled, remain unknown. We analyzed cross-band ISO coupling across six frequency bands during NREM using a wild-type (WT) discovery dataset of 122 recordings from 72 mice and WT validation of 7 mice. A transgenic (TG) validation of 6 mice was added to test ISO coupling's robustness to Cre knock-in on the LepR gene (LepR-Cre). Band power time series were filtered to the ISO range of 0.01-0.03 Hz. Cross-band coupling was assessed using Spearman's correlation and phase-locking value (PLV) across all 15 band pairs. ISOs were strongest in alpha, sigma, beta, and theta bands, weak in gamma, and absent in delta. Alpha, sigma, beta, and theta ISOs formed a highly correlated motif with replication in WT and TG (r = 0.61-0.77), while gamma had moderate correlation (r = 0.30-0.42), and delta was uncorrelated (p > 0.05). All band pairs showed significant phase locking with replication (FDR-corrected q < 0.01), with stronger consistency in alpha, sigma, theta, and beta (PLV 0.54-0.71), and weaker consistency involving delta and gamma (PLV 0.12-0.37). EEG ISOs extend beyond the sigma band to alpha, beta, and theta bands, forming a strongly coupled motif that may reflect a fundamental organization principle of sleep microstructures at a minute scale.

papers.title: Advancing Pediatric Sleep Assessment through Spectral Sleep Scoring: A Comparison with Polysomnography.
papers.abstract: Understanding how sleep changes across development requires methods that are both efficient and sensitive to maturational differences in sleep physiology. Spectral sleep scoring is a promising approach, but has primarily been validated in adult populations. This study presents and validates a spectral scoring approach for pediatric sleep. Participants (n = 192; 9-18y) completed overnight in-lab sleep studies. Visual scoring was determined by registered polysomnographic technologists and confirmed by board certified sleep physicians following AASM guidelines. Visual stages included: wake, non-rapid eye movement (NREM) stage 1 (N1), NREM stage 2 (N2), NREM stage 3 (N3), and rapid-eye movement (REM) sleep. Spectral activity within each epoch was assessed for the following spectral stages: Wake (40-95 Hz), Light (~11- 15.5 Hz), Hi Deep (1-3 Hz), Lo Deep (0.1-1 Hz), and REM (~17-26 Hz). Concordance rates were checked across agreement matrices between visual and spectral stages, with expected high agreement between: 1) visual Wake and spectral Wake; 2) visual N2 and spectral Light; 3) visual N3 and spectral HiDeep/LoDeep; and 4) visual REM and spectral REM. Cohen's κ was calculated from concordance matrices. There was high agreement between visual and spectral stages (71-89%, κ=.76). Our results provide evidence that spectral scoring is a promising method for efficiently scoring pediatric sleep. Moreover, this method provides additional, clinically relevant information that is not readily captured through traditional visual scoring. This may be particularly valuable for assessing sleep physiology in pediatric clinical populations, where developmental differences in EEG patterns may complicate visual scoring.

papers.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a period of distinct maturational changes in sleep physiology. Age-related trends in sleep physiology have been captured using laboratory-based polysomnography, a method limited by logistical burden and high cost. We tested the ability of the Dreem3 sleep EEG headband to replicate established age effects in sleep physiology from late childhood through early adulthood. Typically developing youth (N = 100, 9-26 years) completed 3-4 consecutive nights of at-home sleep recording. We estimated age-related trends across eight macro-architecture and 15 micro-architecture variables with known age effects, and conducted exploratory analyses of 24 additional variables. Dreem3 replicated established age trends, including increases in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) stage 2%, and decreases in N3%, time in bed, NREM delta and theta power with increasing age. Exploratory analysis revealed age effects in twelve additional variables, including decreases in spindle activity with increasing age. Sleep EEG wearables offer an accessible way to characterize sleep physiology development.

papers.title: Reduced-observable dynamic mode decomposition for identifying theta and beta activity in working-memory EEG
papers.abstract: The analysis of transient oscillatory activity in neural recordings remains challenging for linear methods, particularly when signals are nonlinear, noisy, and distributed across multiple channels. This paper introduces a Reduced-Observable Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (RO-eDMD) algorithm using a Random Fourier Features dictionary to characterize high-dimensional data in electroencephalography (EEG) recordings. The method extends the Koopman operator framework by incorporating rank reduction directly in the observable space and employing a randomized feature map that approximates the Gaussian kernel, enabling the capture of transient components without explicit dictionary optimization. To assess the method and demonstrate applicability, a logistic regression model is trained using a working memory paradigm as a test case, using dominant power values extracted via RO-eDMD in the theta band as a predictor and the type of event (encoding vs.\ fixation) as the dependent variable. We find correlations between oscillatory power and memory encoding events in the analyzed bands. Additionally, we find an increase in correlation associated with theta power and memory load, replicating similar results in the literature. The presented algorithm offers a computationally efficient, interpretable framework applied to a working memory paradigm dataset, but is relevant to the analysis of neural time series from diverse experimental contexts.

ai.reason: Introduces a random-feature reduced-observable DMD framework for extracting transient theta/beta oscillations, a transferable spectral/dynamical-systems method relevant to neural time-series analysis.
ai.summary: Introduces Reduced-Observable Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (RO-eDMD) with a Random Fourier Features dictionary to extract transient theta and beta oscillatory power from multichannel working-memory EEG. Using the extracted theta power in a logistic regression, the authors report correlations with encoding events and memory load, replicating prior findings, in a computationally efficient Koopman-based framework.

papers.title: CADENCE: Open-source software for signal conditioning, feature extraction, visualization and analysis of cardiac optical mapping data.
papers.abstract: Optical mapping is a fundamental tool for cardiac electrophysiology research. Processing of these signals can be non-trivial, requiring multiple pre- and post-processing steps to limit interpretation errors. Existing software packages have features siloed across platforms and require users to combine several packages for in-depth analysis. To address this, we developed CADENCE, an open-source MATLAB-based application combining feature breadth (e.g., SVD denoising, conduction velocity, alternans, annotated rotors) and depth (e.g., 15 independent alternans features across both voltage and calcium modalities) in an end-to-end pipeline including data conversion, signal conditioning, feature extraction, and signal analysis. We demonstrate CADENCE's capabilities across datasets spanning four species (rat, rabbit, pig, and human), three tissue preparations (slices, wedge, and whole heart), and three camera configurations (single, dual, and panoramic). CADENCE was validated against three blinded expert observers (15 hearts) and demonstrated agreement comparable to inter-observer variability (SD ratios 1.07/0.95/0.89 for APD80, activation, CaTD80). Dominant frequency was recovered with a median error of 0.03% across 84 of 88 paced recordings with 1:1 capture. CADENCE's code is publicly available and distributed as a compiled standalone application that the end-user can install and run without a MATLAB license to encourage adoption and standardization across laboratories.

papers.title: Channel-Adaptive Temporal Modeling with Grouped Convolutional Network and Informer for Seizure Detection and Prediction.
papers.abstract: Reliable identification and early prediction of epileptic seizures play a critical role in improving patient outcomes and supporting timely therapeutic decision-making. To address the challenges of spatiotemporal feature coupling and long-range dependency modeling in multi-channel EEG signals, this paper proposes a channel-adaptive temporal modeling framework named GCNN-Informer. The framework follows a three-stage pipeline: a grouped convolutional network (GCNN) extracts local features and selects the five most discriminative channels; a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) performs dual spatiotemporal enhancement; and a lightweight Informer encoder captures global temporal dependencies via the ProbSparse self-attention mechanism. Experiments on the CHB-MIT dataset, conducted under a patient-specific evaluation scheme, demonstrated that the proposed method achieved accuracies of 97.33% for seizure detection and 97.28% for seizure prediction, with a low false detection rate (FDR) of 0.30/h and a false prediction rate (FPR) of 0.03/h. Grad-CAM visualization further shows that as EEG signals evolve from normal/interictal to preictal and then to ictal stages, the model's attention heatmap progressively transitions from locally sparse highlighting to continuous block-like highlighting, and finally to dense deep-red responses - a pattern that closely aligns with clinical electrophysiological dynamics. This study provides an accurate and generalizable deep-learning solution for real-time epileptic monitoring and early-warning systems.

ai.summary: Proposed GCNN-Informer, a channel-adaptive deep learning framework combining grouped convolutional networks, CBAM attention, and a lightweight Informer encoder for multi-channel EEG seizure detection and prediction. On the CHB-MIT dataset under patient-specific evaluation, it achieved 97.33% detection accuracy and 97.28% prediction accuracy with low false rates (0.30/h and 0.03/h).

papers.title: A Personalized Approach to Student Mental Health: Real-Time EEG Biofeedback for Stress and Focus Management
papers.abstract: Real-time monitoring of student stress and focus requires low-cost EEG systems, but fixed spectral thresholds may not transfer reliably across users because EEG amplitude and band power vary between individuals and recording conditions. This study investigates a subject-specific thresholding approach using a two-channel Brain BioAmp acquisition setup (FP1 and FP2) and an ESP32-based FFT pipeline. Beta/Alpha and Theta/Alpha ratios are calculated from spectral band estimates and compared with thresholds derived from Baseline, Focused, and Stressed task-condition recordings. In the reported pilot results, the mean Beta/Alpha ratio increased from 2.76 during Baseline to 2.80 during Focused and 2.88 during Stressed conditions. The Theta/Alpha ratio was lowest during Focused (0.95) and highest during Stressed (1.04), compared with 0.99 during Baseline. These are descriptive observations; classification accuracy, statistical significance, and generalization across participants have not been established. The signal-processing calculations and plotted frequency ranges should be checked against the original implementation before these values are treated as final.

papers.title: Longitudinal Imaging in a Mouse Model of Focal Cortical Dysplasia Reveals Lesion Expansion and Loss of Pre-Discharge Neuronal Recruitment
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective: Focal cortical dysplasia type II (FCD II) is a leading cause of drug-resistant focal epilepsy, yet how its lesional circuits behave and change over time in vivo has not been directly observed. Methods: We used a mouse model of FCD II carrying the patient-derived gain-of-function mTORp.L2427P variant introduced by in utero electroporation. Through a chronic cranial window over the lesion, we performed repeated in vivo two-photon calcium imaging of identified dysmorphic neurons, pyramidal cells, and VIP interneurons at defined time points, combined with video-EEG monitoring, to determine seizure status and relate cellular activity to interictal discharges. Results: The lesion was not static in adulthood. Dysplastic cortex expanded progressively. This expansion occurred without the tenascin R/C accumulation reported in human FCD II, and was partly explained by continued somatic growth of dysmorphic neurons. Dysmorphic neurons were generally hypoactive; in seizing mice, both dysmorphic and pyramidal cell activity progressively declined, whereas VIP interneuron activity increased slightly in non-seizing animals. In non-seizing lesional cortex, neurons were reliably recruited immediately before interictal discharges. By late disease stages, pre-discharge recruitment had weakened to the point that lesional layer 2/3 neurons were no more active before discharges than expected by chance. Significance: These findings recast FCD II as a lesion that continues to remodel structurally and functionally throughout adulthood, and does so most markedly in animals with seizures. Growth, a cell-type-specific shift in spontaneous activity, and a progressive loss of the lesion's temporal lead over interictal discharges together suggest that FCD II is a dynamically evolving lesion whose relationship to epileptiform activity changes over time. If the lesion progressively loses its generative role, the window in which removing it can arrest the disease is finite, consistent with clinical evidence favoring earlier surgery.

papers.title: Lifespan Trajectories of Resting State Bipolar EEG Power.
papers.abstract: Normative trajectories of resting state bipolar EEG power over the lifespan were derived from a sample of 5781 participants from the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism (COGA), a large multi site study, using 12,906 observations from ages 12 through 70. Trajectories were analyzed using the means, variances, and correlations of data in seven frequency bands (from low theta to high beta) and 24 bipolar channels obtained from 17 electrodes of the 10-20 system. In order to make the study more useful for understanding EEG in the general population, only subjects never having an alcohol use disorder (AUD) diagnosis were included in the study. Bipolar EEG data is derived from the differencing of the signals in adjacent electrodes, either in a lateral (left-right) or sagittal (anterior-posterior) orientation; each difference is called a channel. The power values for the individual observations were calculated by standard Fourier transform based methods. In all cases there are sharp decreases in EEG power from ages 12 to the early 20s after which there are number of divergent patterns: general increases in the beta frequencies, and mixed patterns of increase and subsequent decrease in the theta and alpha frequencies. In these characteristics the lifespan trajectories presented here are similar to the monopolar trajectories described in our previous study Chorlian et al. (2026). Sagittal and lateral bipolar trajectories are similar within each sex and between sexes; the primary difference is the much lower degree of regional difference in the sagittal trajectories as compared to the lateral trajectories. The pairwise inter-frequency (within channel) correlation trajectories between the four theta and alpha frequency bands and the four high alpha and beta frequency bands at each channel show striking sex differences unlike the corresponding monopolar correlations. There are a number of features in the bipolar power trajectories that suggest that the differencing procedure reduces not only local phase synchrony, but also effects of global and regional phase synchrony present in the monopolar data from which the bipolar signals are derived. The inter-frequency correlations at the individual channels are much higher in the bipolar data than the monopolar data, suggesting that global and regional phase synchrony components retained in the monopolar data have greater frequency specificity than the more purely local components in the bipolar data. Further analyses to examine many other features of the data will be undertaken in our subsequent work.

papers.title: Phase-dependent EEG decoding of continuous visual stimuli.
papers.abstract: Neural oscillations support cognition and perception by organizing information across oscillatory cycles. Although animal studies support this view, evidence in humans is mixed and largely based on transient stimuli. We tested whether alpha oscillations, the dominant human brain rhythm, periodically modulate the strength of visual representations. EEG was recorded while participants viewed long-lasting (2 s) Gabor patches. Using a phase-dependent decoding approach, we quantified stimulus decoding accuracy at specific alpha phases. Decoding performance varied systematically with alpha phase, following a smooth unimodal profile that peaked over occipito-parietal electrodes. These effects emerged well after stimulus onset and generalized to earlier time points, indicating a modulation of visual processing during continuous input. Our findings demonstrate that visual information is represented more accurately at specific alpha phases. This provides strong evidence that sensory processing is shaped by intrinsic brain dynamics and introduces a generalizable decoding pipeline for linking oscillatory phase to neural information processing.

papers.title: Transcranial Evoked Potentials are Minimally Influenced by Afferent Feedback From Peripheral Muscle Contraction.
papers.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation with electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) investigates cortical reactivity, yet the contribution of sensory feedback from muscle twitches to the recorded signals remains debated. We combined M1 TMS-EEG with electromyography, accelerometry, and peripheral electrical stimulation to dissociate central and peripheral contributions. We compared EEG responses across trials yielding large versus small motor outputs, while peripheral stimulation isolated pure afferent components. Bayesian analysis revealed that larger motor outputs covaried with distinct EEG morphologies uniformly across all time windows-including those too early for peripheral feedback-indicating that spontaneous fluctuations in baseline motor cortex excitability drive both responses. Conversely, isolated muscle contraction produced delayed (> 65 ms), markedly smaller EEG responses with distinct spatiotemporal profiles. We conclude that sensory feedback from muscle twitches contributes minimally to TMS-evoked EEG responses, which instead primarily reflect the baseline excitability state of the stimulated cortex.

ai.summary: Combined M1 TMS-EEG with electromyography, accelerometry, and peripheral electrical stimulation to dissociate central from peripheral contributions to TMS-evoked potentials. Larger motor outputs covaried with distinct EEG morphologies across all time windows including pre-feedback latencies, whereas isolated muscle contraction produced only delayed (>65 ms) small responses, indicating TMS-evoked potentials mainly reflect baseline motor cortex excitability.

papers.title: Multimodal evidence associated with 20Hz rTMS in AD: neuroaxonal injury reduction, neural oscillatory rebalancing, and multilayer network integration.
papers.abstract: High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has been demonstrated to enhance cognitive function in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the neurobiological mechanisms associated with neuroaxonal injury, neural oscillatory dynamics, and large-scale network reorganization remain unclear. In this study, we first conducted a randomized, sham-controlled trial with 16 patients with AD to evaluate the efficacy of DLPFC-targeted rTMS, followed by a single-arm multimodal cohort study of 30 patients to explore potential neurobiological mechanisms through cognitive assessments, blood biomarkers, EEG oscillatory activity, and multiplex brain network analysis. In Stage 1, the sham group showed no significant pre-post changes in MMSE or MoCA scores (MMSE: Z = -0.738, Cohen's r = 0.26; MoCA: Z =-0.853, Cohen's r = 0.30). The active rTMS group showed improvements in MMSE (Z = -2.124, Cohen's r = 0.75) and MoCA (Z = -2.108, Cohen's r = 0.75). In stage 2, rTMS was associated with improvements in MMSE (Z = -2.863, Cohen's r = 0.523) and MoCA (t = -6.137, Cohen's r = 0.752) scores. Biomarker analyses indicated a significant decrease in NfL concentrations (Z=-2.371, Cohen's r=0.484). EEG recordings revealed a decrease in delta power in the left temporal lobe (t=2.158, Cohen's r=0.372) and increases in beta power in the right parietal lobe and gamma power in the temporal lobe (beta: Z=-2.088, Cohen's r=0.381; gamma: Z=-2.129, Cohen's r=0.389). Network analysis showed reduced modularity and enhanced global efficiency across theta, alpha, and beta bands, accompanied by increased degree of overlap in frontal, parietal, and occipital regions. Importantly, MoCA improvement correlated with gamma-band global efficiency (R=0.389, P=0.034) and multilayer clustering coefficients in the left frontal and right occipital regions (R=0.478, P=0.008; R=0.398, P=0.029). Overall, rTMS exposure was associated with cognitive improvements in patients with AD, together with changes in neurodegeneration-related biomarkers and EEG network organization. These findings suggest that cognitive changes following rTMS may be associated with oscillatory modulation and large-scale network remodeling. papers.title: A robust adversarial learning framework for EEG emotion recognition.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides an objective means of capturing neural patterns associated with emotion, but substantial inter-subject variability limits the ability of existing models to generalize to unseen subjects. We propose a robust adversarial domain generalization framework for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition. In the first stage, long short-term memory-based encoders are jointly trained to learn domain-invariant and domain-specific representations using reconstruction, emotion classification, and adversarial domain objectives. This process preserves emotion-relevant information while suppressing subject-specific distribution shifts. In the second stage, the invariant encoder and emotion classifier are further refined through distributionally robust optimization with gradient-guided feature augmentation. Theframework is evaluated on the AMIGOS and DREAMER datasets using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The proposed method achieves mean accuracies of 69.94% and 68.97% and F1 scores of 0.59 and 0.65 on AMIGOS and DREAMER, respectively, outperforming the comparison methods on both datasets. Ablation results further show that adversarial learning provides the primary improvement in cross-subject generalization, while distributionally robust optimization offers complementary robustness. These findings indicate that combining representation learning that is invariant across domains with distributionally robust optimization effectively reduces distribution shifts across subjects and improves EEG emotion recognition for unseen subjects.

Under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, the method reached mean accuracies of 69.94% and 68.97% and F1 scores of 0.59 and 0.65 on AMIGOS and DREAMER, outperforming comparison methods, with adversarial learning providing the main generalization gain.

papers.title: Age and sex impact resting-state EEG aperiodic activity beyond symptom associations in persistent post-concussive symptoms
papers.abstract: Objective: to investigate whether resting-state EEG aperiodic parameters (i.e., offset and exponent) are associated with symptom burden and demographic factors in patients with persistent post-concussive symptoms (PPCS) and differ from healthy controls. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, resting-state eye-closed high-density EEG was recorded in patients with PPCS and in age-matched healthy controls. Aperiodic parameters were extracted from EEG power spectra. In patients, hierarchical multiple linear regression models included age and sex as a base model, with additional demographic and clinical symptoms entered separately. Patient-control differences were assessed using multiple linear regression adjusted for age and sex. Results: Seventy patients with PPCS (54 female; 39.57 {+/-}12.21 y.; 109.5 [76.5; 196] days post-concussion) recruited from a concussion care pathway and 38 healthy controls (17 female; 39.61{+/-} 13.57 y.) were included. In patients, younger age and male sex were associated with higher offset and exponent values (all p under .014). None of the additional demographic and clinical variables improved model fit beyond age and sex (all p under.143). After adjustment for age and sex, neither offset (p=.898) nor exponent (p=.100) differed between patients and controls. Conclusion: Resting-state aperiodic EEG parameters were consistently associated with age and sex, but not with self-reported symptom burden or clinical characteristics in patients with PPCS. Not accounting for these factors may generate apparent group differences attributable, at least in part, to demographic variability. Significance: Age and sex are important sources of inter-individual variability in resting-state aperiodic EEG activity and should be systematically considered when investigating such features.

papers.title: Stability of the Epileptogenic Index across seizures and the effects of sleep and withdrawal of anti-seizure medications.
papers.abstract: Epileptogenic Index (EI) is a promising index to evaluate the epileptogenicity of the brain tissue and is useful in planning epilepsy surgery. We aimed to evaluate whether EI maps are consistent across seizures within patients and whether EI-derived measures are affected by the vigilance state and anti-seizure medication (ASM) dose. We analyzed 127 stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) seizures from 19 patients. EI was calculated in all seizures. Within-patient EI consistency was assessed using pairwise Spearman correlations between seizure-specific EI maps. To assess the effects of vigilance and ASM on EI consistency, we calculated a contact-level p_weighted EI score that combines the frequency of suprathreshold EI involvement and mean EI magnitude, separately across vigilance states and in a subset of patients with different ASM states. Mean seizure-to-seizure EI correlations ranged from 0.11 to 0.81, indicating substantial variability in within-patient EI consistency. Seven patients showed high consistency (≥0.6) and four showed low consistency (≤0.3). At the contact level, no differences in p_weighted EI were found between wakefulness and sleep. In contrast, p_weighted EI was significantly higher during reduced ASM compared with full ASM doses. EI maps are not uniformly stable across seizures. ASM reduction may broaden or intensify EI-defined epileptogenic involvement, suggesting that ASM status should be considered when interpreting EI during SEEG evaluation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation to determine their clinical utility for surgical planning. The Epileptogenic Index (EI) measures the involvement of a recorded brain area during a specific seizure. This study shows that EI patterns can vary significantly between different seizures in the same patient. While sleep states do not change these patterns, reducing a patient's anti-seizure medications increases EI values, making seizures appear to spread more broadly. These medication-induced changes must be carefully considered to accurately map the epileptic network for surgical decisions.

papers.title: A Novel Digital Phenotype of Physical Activity: Associations with Heart Rate Fragmentation.
papers.abstract: Heart rate fragmentation (HRF) has emerged as a novel marker of sinoatrial instability and neuroautonomic dysregulation and is a predictor of incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) events and cardiovascular mortality. Leveraging heart rate fragmentation as a novel measure may help us better understand the prognostic significance of physical activity. Physical activity (PA) patterns are multidimensional and difficult to study holistically, however. We sought to examine for novel PA clusters in a cohort of veteran men and evaluate their prognostic significance based on their associations with neuroautonomic dysregulation. In this cross-sectional study, we examined 602 male veterans from the Vietnam Era Twins Study of Electrophysiology in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (VETS-EP) who were enrolled between 2022 and 2026. Accelerometry data were used to derive physical activity parameters across 6 domains: volume, sedentary behavior, intensity, diurnal pattern, fragmentation, and variability. Heart rate fragmentation was assessed using percentage of inflection points (PIP), inverse average length of segments (IALS), percentage of short segments (PSS), and percentage of alternating segments (PAS). Gaussian mixture models were used to derive digital phenotypes of physical activity, and associations with heart rate fragmentation were assessed using linear mixed models. Participants had a mean age of 73.8 ± 2.9 years and 93.2% reported White race. Two overlapping phenotypes of physical activity patterns were identified: a compact-early phenotype, characterized by earlier activity timing and slightly greater overall activity, and a diffuse-late phenotype, characterized by later activity timing and greater heterogeneity in activity volume. In fully adjusted models, the diffuse-late phenotype was associated with higher PIP, the primary outcome (β: 1.199, 95% CI: 0.034 to 2.363, p-value: 0.044), and higher IALS (β: 0.01210, 95% CI: 0.00048 to 0.02373, p-value: 0.041), but not PSS or PAS, compared with the compact-early phenotype. In older male veterans, Gaussian mixture model phenotyping identified two overlapping physical activity phenotypes, differing mainly in diurnal timing and in the dispersion of overall activity, that were associated with modest differences in heart rate fragmentation. These phenotypes provide a framework for capturing complex physical activity patterns. Future prospective studies representing diverse populations are needed to validate such phenotypes.

papers.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles.
papers.abstract: Black participants remain underrepresented in electroencephalography (EEG) research, partly because current EEG devices work poorly with dense, coily Type 4 Afro-textured hair. Research-grade EEG typically wires electrodes on a cap, and therefore the electrodes often fail to reach the scalp through dense, Afro-textured hair. Protocols that ask Black participants to unbraid or restyle protective hairstyles add burdens that discourage enrollment in research studies. To address this, we designed and tested 3D-printed attachments that fit onto an EEG electrode and anchored it directly in the hair, using the hairstyle itself as the mounting structure. We fabricated three design configurations for natural Afro-textured hair, cornrows/braids, and twists/microlocs. Seventeen healthy adults with Type 4a-4c hair used electrode attachments that matched their hairstyle. During a single visit, EEG was recorded with 16 conventional cap electrodes defined by the international 10-20 system and with 16 electrodes using novel electrode attachments anchored directly to their hair. Participants completed resting and walking trials with each system. Electrode-to-scalp distance and gel volume were measured during setup. Electrode disconnection, impedance, signal quality (i.e. peak alpha power and aperiodic (1/f) component), and comfort level were measured throughout the data collection. Compared with the conventional cap, the novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance. Twenty percent of the conventional cap electrodes failed to connect to the scalp compared with 0.1% of novel electrodes. Impedance rose across trials for the conventional cap, whereas the novel attachments showed a smaller increase and maintained lower impedance throughout. Signal quality was significantly better using the novel attachments, while comfort level did not differ between systems. In conclusion, hair-anchored electrode attachment may present a feasible alternative to conventional cap-based EEG for people with Type 4 hair, yielding more usable channels and better signal quality, and supporting more inclusive EEG acquisition.

papers.title: Elevated neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility in a mouse model of SCN2A -related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic variants in SCN2A cause a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders, including developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE). The patient-associated SCN2A -p.E430A variant selectively shifts voltage-dependence of activation, a mechanism predicted to enhance neuronal excitability. To investigate the functional consequences of the SCN2A -E430A variant, we generated the novel Scn2a E430A mouse model and assessed neuronal excitability, brain activity, seizure susceptibility, and phenytoin responsiveness. Heterozygous Scn2a E430A mice retained normal Scn2a expression levels and did not exhibit premature lethality. Hippocampal pyramidal neurons from heterozygous Scn2a E430A mice were hyperexcitable compared to wild-type neurons. Enhanced long-term potentiation was observed in the CA1 circuit of Scn2a E430A mice. Video-EEG data revealed recurrent epileptiform discharges and spectral abnormalities, but no spontaneous generalized seizure events. In multiple seizure-induction assays, Scn2a E430A mice had no difference in latency to first seizure signs, but exhibited faster seizure generalization and more lethality compared to wild-type mice, indicating alterations in seizure propagation and/or cessation rather than seizure initiation. Pretreatment with phenytoin improved seizure outcomes across all seizure induction methods. Together, these findings demonstrate that selective disruption of Scn2a activation gating is sufficient to drive neuronal hyperexcitability and network dysfunction, establishing the Scn2a E430A mouse as clinically relevant and pharmacologically tractable model of SCN2A -related DEE.

papers.title: A behavioral and electrophysiological study on the influence of menstrual cycle, estradiol and progesterone on the social approach-avoidance behavior tendencies of women.
papers.abstract: It remains unclear whether women's social approach-avoidance behaviors toward different facial expressions are influenced by their menstrual cycles, estradiol and progesterone levels, or what the underlying electrophysiological mechanisms might be. This study collected data on the levels of estradiol and progesterone, social approach-avoidance behavior and electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings from 27 women with natural menstrual cycles during three phases- early follicular phase, late follicular phase, and mid-luteal phase. The results showed that women in the late follicular phase exhibited a faster approach tendency and a smaller LPP amplitude to happy faces compared to the early follicular phase; women in the mid-luteal phase exhibited a faster approach tendency and a smaller LPP amplitude to fearful faces compared to the late follicular phase. Estradiol levels is positively correlated with the efficiency of approach behavior toward happy faces, while progesterone levels is positively correlated with the efficiency of approach behavior toward fearful faces. The results show that women's social approach-avoidance behaviors are specifically regulated by the menstrual cycle, estradiol and progesterone, and exhibit higher cognitive processing efficiency in the late positive potential (LPP) of the brain. These findings are manifestations in social interactions of the characteristics of women's interest pursuit and self-restraint under the influence of different sex hormones formed during evolution, updating established hormone-behavior links in social emotional contexts.

papers.title: Vibrotactile transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) during working memory: convergent electrophysiological evidence for cortical efficiency.
papers.abstract: Working memory, the cognitive ability to maintain and manipulate a finite amount of information, is fundamental in reasoning, learning, and decision-making. Working memory erodes in conditions from Alzheimer's disease to stroke to healthy aging. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a promising neuromodulation method for improving working memory. By stimulating the auricular branch of the vagus nerve, taVNS is thought to engage ascending arousal systems such as the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine (LC-NE) system. However, the physiological link between LC-NE system modulation via taVNS and improved working memory remains largely unknown. This mechanistic gap limits the rational optimization of the stimulation protocol and the identification of the cognitive functions and patient populations that are likely to benefit. We test two competing hypotheses for how taVNS may improve working memory: sensory amplification or enhancement of cortical efficiency. The sensory-amplification hypothesis predicts increased cortical responses to stimuli, whereas the cortical-efficiency hypothesis predicts reduced cortical responses. Twenty healthy adults completed N-back working memory tasks during three counterbalanced sessions: baseline, active vibrotactile taVNS (vtaVNS), and sham stimulation, while we simultaneously recorded electroencephalography, electrocardiography, eye-tracking, and behavioral responses. To study the effect of vtaVNS on neuronal activity, we also recruited 20 patients with epilepsy undergoing invasive monitoring. Of these, 19 fully completed the spatial working-memory task. We quantified cortical responses to visual stimuli using event-related potentials (ERPs) in scalp EEG and high-gamma activity in intracranial local field potentials. To examine prediction of the cortical-efficiency hypothesis, we further explored the effect of vtaVNS on distance to criticality and heartbeat-evoked potentials. Active vtaVNS reduced both scalp-recorded visual ERP and high-gamma response in temporal cortices, relative to sham stimulation. Moreover, smaller visual event-related potentials were associated with successful encoding during the most demanding working-memory condition (i.e., 4-back task). Exploratory analyses showed that vtaVNS shifted cortical dynamics closer to criticality. Our results converge on the conclusion that vtaVNS does not uniformly amplify cortical responses to external stimuli. Instead, vtaVNS enhances cortical efficiency, supporting more effective allocation of cognitive resources between exteroceptive and mnemonic processes. These findings provide a framework for predicting when taVNS will be most beneficial and for optimizing stimulation protocols across cognitive and clinical applications. papers.title: Seizures induce c-fos expression in a subset of astrocytes, termed fostrocytes, that dampen subsequent seizures.
papers.abstract: The original goal was to map neuronal circuits activated by spontaneous seizures in models of temporal lobe epilepsy. Studies used the c-fos driven TRAP2 system, which has been used successfully to label neurons after seizures. Unexpectedly, astrocytes were also labeled, then shown to express c-fos in a sustained manner after seizures. The role of these so-called fostrocytes in spontaneous seizures was studied using novel Cre-dependent AAVs. Studies used a homozygous mouse line produced by crossing TRAP2 Cre-driver mice with the Ai9 Cre-reporter line. Seizures were induced using electrical stimulation, kainic acid, or pilocarpine. Cre-dependent AAVs used the GFAP promoter to drive expression of either the catalytic A chain of diphtheria toxin (DTA), GFP, or empty vector. Spontaneous seizures were continuously recorded using EEG. Discrete seizures in naïve mice evoked transient c-fos expression in all astrocytes, while status epilepticus evoked a higher and sustained level of c-fos expression. Timing the activation of the TRAP2 system allowed specific labeling of the subset of astrocytes with high c-fos expression. These cells were colocalized with established astrocyte markers, showed reactive astrocyte morphology, and were selectively labeled by GFAP-driven Cre-dependent AAVs. Ablation of fostrocytes in spontaneously seizing mice increased seizure frequency. Next-generation sequencing studies have revealed a great diversity of astrocyte subtypes, identifying clusters with up-regulated c-fos expression in patients with neurological disorders. In conclusion, these studies suggest that therapies that augment the activity of c-fos expressing astrocytes would have anti-seizure activity. ➢ Discrete seizures triggered a transient expression of c-fos in all astrocytes, while status epilepticus triggered its prolonged expression in a subset of astrocytes.➢ The TRAP2 system expresses inducible Cre recombinase controlled by the Fos gene, providing genetic access to astrocytes that express c-fos at high levels.➢ Cre-dependent delivery of a diphtheria toxin selectively ablated these fostrocytes and exacerbated spontaneous seizures.➢ Novel therapies that augment the activity of fostrocytes are predicted to reduce seizure burden.

papers.title: A screening method for aortic valve disease based on spectral analysis of a single-channel electrocardiogram using machine learning algorithms.

For moderate or severe aortic regurgitation, accuracy was 0.726 (Se 60.5%, Sp 73.3%) for Balanced Random Forest and 0.712 (Se 61.7%, Sp 71.9%) for XGBoost. papers.title: Developmental mechanisms contributing to non-linear firing dynamics in spinal motoneurons of the postnatal mouse.
papers.abstract: The intrinsic properties of spinal motoneurons support flexible movement, including the maintenance of postural tone. Motoneurons can produce sustained action potential output that outlasts synaptic input, a phenomenon traditionally attributed to persistent inward currents (PICs) mediated by sodium and calcium channels. Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology, we examined how specific ion channels contribute to PIC maturation and non-linear firing dynamics that allow motoneurons to sustain their output in fast and slow lumbar motoneurons across postnatal development in mice. PIC amplitude and non-linear firing dynamics increased after weight-bearing in fast but not slow motoneurons. Blocking NaV1.6 channels reduced PIC amplitude at both pre- and post-weight-bearing stages, whereas L-type calcium channel blockade only reduced PICs after weight-bearing emerged. However, reducing PIC amplitude by blocking these channels, either individually or in parallel, did not abolish sustained firing hysteresis, which may be because PICs are not yet fully established at this stage of postnatal development. Unexpectedly, activation of muscarinic receptors increased PIC amplitude while promoting adaptive firing dynamics, suggesting that PICs alone do not account for sustained firing hysteresis. We also found that pharmacological manipulation of potassium currents mediated by KCNQ and KV1.2 channels produced substantial changes in firing dynamics. Strikingly, blocking hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels promoted sustained firing dynamics and led to the emergence of self-sustained firing in fast motoneurons. These results indicate that PICs and non-linear firing dynamics mature together and extend the current framework on non-linear firing dynamics of motoneurons to include additional voltage-gated ion channels. Increased expression or function of L-type calcium channels may contribute to enhanced PIC amplitude in fast motoneurons after weight-bearing emerges. Blocking NaV1.6 or L-type calcium channels did not reduce sustained firing hysteresis in fast motoneurons. KCNQ channels oppose PICs and, together with KV1.2 channels, shape recruitment-derecruitment asymmetry, thereby modulating firing hysteresis in fast motoneurons. Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels generate a resting H-current that delays recruitment, modulates firing hysteresis, and prevents the emergence of self-sustained firing in fast motoneurons.

This retrospective observational cohort study was conducted at a tertiary pediatric neurophysiology and neurology center. Patients aged 1-18 years fulfilling current International League Against Epilepsy criteria for LGS were identified through local databases. All available sleep video-EEG recordings before November 2024 were reviewed; clinical features, EEG findings, and comorbidities were collected at each recording. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. We reviewed 234 EEGs from 51 patients (75% male). Median age at first EEG was 5 years. GPFA emerged later than slow spike-and-wave (mean age: 9.6 vs 8.3 years, p = 0.002), with non-parametric analysis confirming a significant difference in age at first detection (p = 0.004). papers.title: How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The effects of school-based interventions (SBIs) on children's neurodevelopment are poorly synthesized. This systematic review integrates neuroscientific evidence on how structured educational activities influence brain development in children aged 3-12 years. Following PRISMA guidelines, we identified 17 empirical studies (published 2014-2025) using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). Of these, 8 studies were included in a random-effects meta-analysis and all 17 in a thematic synthesis. The meta-analysis revealed a preliminary association between SBIs and reduced amygdala activity during stress regulation tasks (r = -.28, 95% CI [-.50, -.02]), based on two studies, which should be interpreted as exploratory rather than confirmatory. No significant pooled effect for executive function, likely due to high heterogeneity. Thematic analysis distinguishes between mechanisms of plasticity and markers of intervention effectiveness: the first three characterize intra-individual mechanisms of experience-dependent plasticity, including (1) executive function interventions engaged prefrontal networks through both increased recruitment and enhanced neural efficiency; (2) socio-emotional programs modulated limbic-prefrontal circuits; (3) language and auditory programs shaped sensory-specific electrophysiological markers and cortical specialization; and the fourth theme identifies a neural marker of the effective process of intervention delivery, demonstrating that (4) teacher-child inter-brain synchrony was positively correlated with learning outcomes. By integrating findings across neural, cognitive, and affective domains, this review provides a conceptual framework linking pedagogical practices to neural plasticity and advances the understanding of the neurofunctional pathways through which educational experiences shape the developing brain.

papers.title: Axonal dysfunction precedes axonal degeneration in a mouse model of progressive parkinsonism.

Our experiments show a pronounced reduction in action potential (AP)-evoked calcium signals in MitoPark axons that emerges well before the onset of dopaminergic fiber loss and motor deficits. In addition, calcium imaging and direct axon recording revealed deficits in AP propagation accompanied by alterations in the axonal AP waveform. Therefore, our experimental findings identify the progression of axon-specific physiological deficits that occur long before neurodegeneration, more precisely defining the period that precedes axonal loss.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Automated Mass Spectral Analysis Using NucleoSpec for Compositional Assignment of Nucleic Acid-Silver Complexes and Nanoclusters.
papers.abstract: Nucleic acid-metal complexes, such as DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters (DNA-Ag N ) and Ag-(I)-mediated DNA duplexes, show promise for applications ranging from biomedical imaging to bioelectronics and sensing. Electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) is a powerful tool for precisely resolving their compositions, but the data analysis procedure can be challenging and time-consuming. No general-purpose software can automatically assign compositions of nucleic acid-silver complexes, most notably for DNA-Ag N , whose masses depend on the oxidation state of the silver core. We address these challenges by developing an automated data analysis workflow for ESI-MS of nucleic acid-silver complexes. This tutorial presents the analysis workflow and introduces NucleoSpec, an open-source, web-based platform that consolidates charge state determination, constraint-based composition enumeration, isotope-pattern matching, and adduct/conjugate handling into a single browser-accessible interface. The platform is benchmarked on published molecular formulas determined by manual analysis for DNA-Ag N , xeno-nucleic acid stabilized Ag N (XNA-Ag N ), nucleic acid-Ag-(I) complexes, and chemically modified DNA-Ag N , reproducing assignments to single-proton precision (median centroid offset of 0.03 m/z) for spectra of adequate signal-to-noise. Low-signal peaks for which adjacent valence electron counts become difficult to distinguish are flagged by NucleoSpec for user inspection. By lowering the barrier to high-resolution compositional analysis and supporting integration into high-throughput pipelines, NucleoSpec addresses a key experimental bottleneck in informatics-guided design of nucleic acid-metal complexes.

papers.title: Effect of epidural spinal cord stimulation combined with personalized neurorehabilitation in chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury: study protocol for the phase II single-arm feasibility RESTORES (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) trial.
papers.abstract: Chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury (SCI) results in profound neurological disability with minimal prospects for functional recovery using conventional rehabilitation strategies. Emerging evidence suggests that epidural spinal cord stimulation (eSCS) can activate dormant spinal locomotor networks and restore volitional and autonomic functions when combined with intensive activity-based training. However, systematic evaluation of multimodal neuromodulation approaches integrating advanced rehabilitation and computational neurophysiology remains limited. The RESTORES trial (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) is a prospective, single-arm Phase II feasibility study enrolling 15 adults with chronic (≥1 year) motor-complete SCI (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment scale (AIS) A or B) between C5 and T12. Participants will undergo implantation of an epidural spinal cord stimulator followed by a 24-week program of structured stimulation-coupled personalised neurorehabilitation (five sessions per week). Clinical outcomes will be evaluated using standardized neurological and functional measures including the AIS motor score, Spinal Cord Independence Measure version III (SCIM-III), Walking Index for Spinal Cord Injury II (WISCI-II), and Trunk Assessment Scale (TASS). Autonomic function and quality of life will also be assessed. Multimodal neurophysiological measurements-including surface electromyography (sEMG), electroencephalography (EEG), resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI), and computer-vision-based movement analysis-will be performed to investigate neural recovery mechanisms and inform the development of adaptive neuromodulation systems. The primary outcome is the safety of epidural spinal cord stimulation implantation, defined as the absence of device explantation for safety-related reasons within 6 months following implantation. Secondary outcomes include changes in AIS motor score, functional outcomes (SCIM, WISCI-II, TASS), autonomic function, quality of life, and neurophysiological biomarkers. This study integrates neuromodulation, advanced rehabilitation technologies, and multimodal computational neurophysiology to evaluate both clinical efficacy and neural mechanisms of recovery following chronic SCI. Findings from the RESTORES trial will provide critical safety and feasibility data to inform future multicenter trials and the development of closed-loop spinal cord stimulation systems. papers.title: Case Report: An MDT-guided multimodal protocol for large-area stroke plateau - integrating neuromodulation with multimodal assessment.
papers.abstract: This case report investigates the feasibility and potential value of an individualized precision rehabilitation protocol for large-area stroke, integrating multimodal neuromodulation under the guidance of a multidisciplinary team (MDT) and dynamic assessment. A 38-year-old male with right hemiplegia and global aphasia following large left hemispheric infarction underwent an 8-month MDT-managed program. A closed-loop "assess-decide-intervene-re-assess" framework was implemented, featuring periodic multimodal evaluations (clinical scales, DTI, fMRI, EEG, 3D gait analysis). The intervention dynamically combined conventional therapy with staged neuromodulation: repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) for aphasia and intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation (iTBS) for motor disorder, Brain-Computer Interface (BCI)-robotic training and task-oriented Virtual Reality (VR) for upper limb function, and biomechanical correction with custom insoles based on gait analysis. Notable functional improvements were observed: LOTCA increased by 16 points, CRRCAE subscale improved by 60%-90%, FMA increased from 20 to 56, FMA-B reached 12, and MBI improved from 40 to 91. Neuroimaging revealed increased fractional anisotropy (FA) in the corpus callosum and right corticospinal tract, and elevated ALFF/ReHo in right frontal-temporal areas. Event-related desynchronization (ERD) decreased during BCI training, and gait parameters improved. In this patient with large-area stroke who showed limited response to conventional rehabilitation, an MDT-guided, dynamically adjusted multimodal intervention was temporally associated with concurrent recovery across cognitive, language, motor, and daily living domains. The concomitant neural changes suggest possible trans-hemispheric network reorganization. These observations are hypothesis-generating and, while limited by the single-case design, provide a preliminary rationale for future investigations into precision neurorehabilitation approaches in similar complex cases. papers.title: Implementation and early experience with tubular retractor-assisted minimally invasive parafascicular surgery for deep brain tumors.
papers.abstract: Minimally invasive parafascicular surgery using tubular retractors (tr-MIPS) has emerged as a strategy to access deep intra-axial lesions while minimizing white matter disruption. However, practical guidance on institutional implementation and integration with modern intraoperative adjuncts remains limited. We describe our early institutional experience with tr-MIPS, with a focus on workflow adoption, multimodal adjunct integration, and feasibility. Demographic, radiographic, operative, and postoperative data were collected, with particular attention to extent of resection, neurological outcomes, and use of adjunctive technologies. Six patients underwent tr-MIPS for deep intra-axial tumors of varied histology. Gross or near-total resection was achieved in four cases. Five patients experienced no new postoperative neurological deficits, and one had transient dysphasia. Median length of stay was 3.5 days. A range of adjuncts including diffusion tensor imaging, 5-aminolevulinic acid fluorescence, intraoperative neurophysiologic monitoring, and depth-electrode electroencephalography were successfully incorporated without workflow disruption. Notably, intraoperative depth-electrode EEG was used to guide resection of an epileptogenic lesion, representing a novel adjunctive application in the tr-MIPS setting. tr-MIPS can be implemented within a modern neurosurgical practice and feasibly integrated with multiple intraoperative adjuncts. We demonstrate feasibility with the addition of this technique to our center's armamentarium. Beyond facilitating access to deep lesions, its compatibility with technologies such as tractography, neurophysiologic monitoring, and EEG expands its functional utility. These findings support the feasibility of a broader adoption of tr-MIPS and highlight opportunities for multimodal, precision-guided minimally invasive neuro-oncologic surgery.

papers.title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in a Pacemaker-Dependent Child with Syndromic Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: A Case Report with Prospective 9-Month Follow-Up.
papers.abstract: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is an emerging noninvasive neuromodulation therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). However, evidence regarding its use in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices, particularly pacemaker-dependent children, remains extremely limited. We report a 6-year-old boy with genetically confirmed TAF6-related Alazami-Yuan syndrome, severe developmental impairment, complete atrioventricular block requiring permanent epicardial VVIR pacing, and syndromic DRE refractory to multiple antiseizure medications (ASMs). Auricular taVNS was initiated at the cymba conchae under multidisciplinary supervision using stimulation parameters of 25 Hz, pulse width 250 μs, intensity titrated to tolerance up to 1.7 mA, for 4 h/day. Treatment initiation was performed in the pediatric intensive care unit with continuous electrocardiographic monitoring for 5 days. The patient underwent prospective follow-up over 9 months using caregiver-maintained seizure diaries, serial electroencephalography (EEG), serial electrocardiography, repeated pacemaker interrogation, adverse event surveillance, and Pediatric Quality of Life Family Impact Module (PedsQL-FIM) assessments. No arrhythmias, pacing abnormalities, device malfunction, or clinically significant pacemaker parameter changes were observed during follow-up. A mild transient local skin irritation resolved with conservative care. Seizure burden decreased from 2 to 4 prolonged seizures daily at baseline to approximately two brief generalized tonic seizures weekly, with sustained improvement through month 9. Reduction of ASM burden began only after clinical improvement had already been observed. Follow-up EEGs remained markedly abnormal with only limited interval electrographic change. PedsQL-FIM improved progressively from 10.4 at baseline to 54.9 at month 3, 80.6 at month 7, and 84.0 at month 9. Auricular taVNS was successfully administered in a pacemaker-dependent child under structured multidisciplinary monitoring without identifiable cardiac or pacemaker-related adverse events during 9 months of follow-up. Although efficacy and safety conclusions cannot be inferred from a single case, this report supports the clinical feasibility of combining noninvasive vagal neuromodulation with permanent cardiac pacing in carefully selected pediatric patients.

papers.title: Real time quantification of carbohydrates in beer wort by FTIR and neural network analysis.
papers.abstract: The brewing process of wort has been predominantly empirical, once that just after the production of a batch is possible to evaluate the performance of raw materials, and if its necessary makes adjustments for the next batches. In this context, the real time information about the composition of the beer wort can facilitate the implemention of modifications during the process to improve both efficiency and precision of the desired physicochemical profile. Thus, this work shows the development of an equipment and signal processing that combines three techniques for monitoring the mashing process in beer production. Real-time quantification of carbohydrates produced by enzymatic reactions between barley malt enzymes and starch during the saccharification step, which is usually achieved through spectral analysis using Fourier transform infrared absorption in the mid-infrared region through collection and referring samples in real time. The system incorporates principal component analysis and artificial neural networks for data processing, however by implementing a flow measurement system controlled by software, the concentration of major carbohydrates (glucose, maltose, maltotriose, and dextrins) in the wort can be quantified during the enzymatic reactions in real time. These measurements offer new possibilities for process control, error reduction, and optimization of reactions as needed, allowing fine control of the process. The real time spectroscopy will provide the application of machine learning tools in the process. While the device and procedure is demonstrated for the efficient control of the beer production, its context and applicability goes much beyond such applications. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13197-024-06128-4.

papers.title: Epilepsy as a consequence of infantile vitamin B12 deficiency: observations from a prospective cohort study and a review of the literature.
papers.abstract: Symptomatic infantile vitamin B12 deficiency has far-reaching neurological consequences for affected children. Development of epilepsy is one such consequence whose incidence and characteristics have been scarcely studied and reported in the literature. To describe the incidence, characteristics, and outcomes of epilepsy in a prospective cohort of children treated for infantile vitamin B12 deficiency and to briefly review the published literature on the topic. A hospital-based prospective cohort study enrolling consecutive children with symptomatic infantile vitamin B12 deficiency was conducted from January 2021 to June 2023 to study the neurological consequences of deficiency. The cohort was followed through March 2026 to determine the incidence of epilepsy during follow-up. Those who developed epilepsy were evaluated for seizure and epilepsy types, neuroimaging and electroencephalography findings, treatment, response to treatment, and outcomes. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling was performed using baseline predictors identified through univariate screening to determine independent associations with epilepsy. A total of 141 children with infantile vitamin B12 deficiency were part of the original cohort. Four died, 25 were lost to follow-up. Among the rest of the 112 children, at a median follow-up of 51 months (IQR: 45-55), 31 (28, 95% CI 19-36%) developed epilepsy. In those with epilepsy, the mean age at diagnosis of infantile vitamin B12 deficiency was 12.39 ± 3.9 months, and epilepsy developed after a mean interval of 4.7 ± 3.2 months after treatment. Epileptic spasms were the most common seizure type (15/31, 48.4%), while other forms of epilepsy were observed in 16. Of the 31, at last contact, 21 (68%) had either resolved or well-controlled epilepsy, 8 (26%) had drug-refractory epilepsy, and 2 (6%) died. In the multivariate model, acute-phase seizures were strongly associated with increased epilepsy risk (pooled HR 4.27, 95% CI:1.6-11.5, p = 0.004). Higher follow-up DQ was protective (pooled HR 0.94, 95% CI:0.89-0.99, p = 0.015). There was an early clustering of epilepsy, with all events occurring within 10 months of follow-up. Epilepsy is a significant neurological outcome of vitamin B12 deficiency in infants. There is early clustering of epilepsy risk after treatment for deficiency, and acute-phase seizures are the strongest independent predictor of later epilepsy.

papers.title: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: To summarize the clinical manifestations, ancillary examination findings, treatment course, and prognosis of a patient with neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis presenting with prominent psychiatric disturbances and choreiform movements, and to review the literature on the clinical spectrum of this disease. A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and biopsy-proven podocytopathy with a "full-house" immunofluorescence pattern showing diffuse positivity for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q, diagnosed in February 2026; however, a definitive diagnosis of lupus podocytopathy remained uncertain, as the patient lacked systemic lupus erythematosus manifestations. She was admitted on April 3, 2026, with a 5-day history of psychiatric disturbances and involuntary choreiform movements in all four limbs, preceded by significant psychological stress (bereavement). Neurological examination revealed slowed responses and impaired calculation. Cranial MRI showed only bilateral periventricular small ischemic foci (Fazekas grade 1) with normal SWI. Initial EEG demonstrated sharp waves and spike-and-wave complexes in the left parietal, occipital, and temporal regions. CSF analysis revealed leukocytosis (21/μl, 90% mononuclear cells), protein of 0.4 g/L, elevated IgG index of 0.76, and elevated 24-hour intrathecal IgG synthesis rate of 5.63 mg/dl. CSF mNGS detected 453 EBV sequences (RPM) with a relative abundance of 97.48%. Serum EBV VCA-IgG and EBNA-IgG were elevated with negative IgM. Autoantibody testing followed a stepwise approach: initial screening for conventional autoimmune encephalitis, paraneoplastic, and demyelinating antibodies was negative; subsequent tissue-based assay (TBA) of CSF revealed strong positive immunoreactivity, prompting expanded antibody panel testing, which ultimately detected anti-neurexin-3α antibodies in serum (titer 1:30) and CSF (titer 1:100), confirmed by both cell-based assay (CBA) and TBA. The patient's condition progressively deteriorated, requiring endotracheal intubation on April 21 and tracheostomy on April 30. She received methylprednisolone pulse therapy at 500 mg/day for 5 days followed by a stepwise taper, intravenous immunoglobulin at 0.4 g/kg for 5 days, and five sessions of plasma exchange from April 30 to May 8 due to poor initial response. Choreiform movements gradually resolved after plasma exchange. She was weaned from mechanical ventilation on May 19 and decannulated on May 27. During the ICU course, she developed pulmonary infection with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which was controlled after antibiotic adjustment. Repeat EEG normalized on June 1. She was discharged from rehabilitation on June 9 on oral methylprednisolone 32 mg/day. On June 26, 2026, follow-up serum TBA showed weakly positive immunoreactivity, with the serum antibody titer remaining at 1:30. She subsequently received four infusions of efgartigimod at 400 mg each for consolidation immunotherapy and was transitioned to ofatumumab for long-term maintenance. At follow-up on August 6, 2026, the patient had no residual psychiatric symptoms or choreiform movements, with muscle strength recovered to 4+ in all limbs, full independence in daily activities, ambulation without assistance, and only mild gait instability. Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis is a rare but treatable condition. Choreiform movements expand its clinical spectrum. The coexistence of podocytopathy raises a hypothesis of shared antigenicity between renal and neuronal neurexin family members, though this remains purely speculative. CSF EBV reactivation may represent a bystander phenomenon or epiphenomenon of severe immune dysregulation rather than a confirmed trigger. Tissue-based assay provides crucial diagnostic direction when conventional screening is negative. Early recognition, comprehensive immunotherapy, and meticulous ICU management are important determinants of favorable outcomes. Given the inherent limitations of a single case report, these findings warrant confirmation through larger cohort studies.

papers.title: Parathyroid Storm Secondary to a Parathyroid Adenoma Presenting With Recurrent Generalised Tonic-Clonic Seizures and Refractory Hypercalcaemia: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Parathyroid storm is a rare, life-threatening manifestation of primary hyperparathyroidism characterised by severe hypercalcaemia and acute multisystem deterioration. We report a 70-year-old woman with known primary hyperparathyroidism who presented with progressive weakness, confusion and reduced mobility and was found to have a corrected serum calcium concentration of 4.14 mmol/L. Despite aggressive intravenous hydration, she developed recurrent generalised tonic-clonic seizures, hypoventilation and reduced consciousness, requiring intubation and intensive care admission. Electroencephalography demonstrated severe diffuse cerebral dysfunction consistent with metabolic encephalopathy, while cerebrospinal fluid studies were unremarkable. Four-dimensional computed tomography of the neck identified a 1.8 cm right-sided parathyroid lesion. Hypercalcaemia remained difficult to control despite multimodal medical therapy, including pamidronate, calcitonin, cinacalcet and denosumab, with recurrent rebound hypercalcaemia. Urgent parathyroidectomy resulted in sustained normalisation of serum calcium and cessation of seizure activity, and histopathology confirmed a benign parathyroid adenoma. This case highlights the severe neurological complications of parathyroid storm and the importance of early multidisciplinary consideration of definitive surgery when hypercalcaemia remains refractory to intensive medical therapy.

papers.title: A SynNotch-PiggyBac gene circuit for inflammation-responsive IL-10 delivery in Alzheimer's disease: a hypothesis and design framework.
papers.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation driven by sustained microglial and astrocyte activation contributes to Alzheimer's disease progression, yet no therapeutic strategy addresses it with precision or durability in the brain. Interleukin-10 occupies an unresolved position in this problem. Constitutive interleukin-10 overexpression in amyloid precursor protein transgenic mice increased plaque burden by suppressing microglial phagocytic activity, while interleukin-10 deletion has been reported to restrict amyloidosis in one setting and to worsen tau hyperphosphorylation in another. We interpret this pattern as evidence that interleukin-10 carries opposite signs on the two principal pathologies of Alzheimer's disease, so that any therapy holding it at a fixed concentration is committed in advance to being wrong about one of them. We therefore propose a falsifiable hypothesis: conditional, inflammation-gated interleukin-10 expression may suppress damaging inflammatory signaling while limiting the impairment of microglial phagocytosis associated with continuous exposure. We present a design framework for a synthetic gene circuit combining an adeno-associated viral vector for delivery to the central nervous system, a synthetic Notch receptor that detects membrane-bound tumor necrosis factor alpha on activated microglia through juxtacrine contact, and a PiggyBac transposon intended to integrate the circuit into the astrocyte genome. Receptor engagement is expected to release a transcription factor that drives interleukin-10 from a synthetic promoter, with transcription ceasing as the stimulus is withdrawn. We provide a quantitative packaging analysis showing that the circuit requires a compacted vector design to fit within viral capacity, and we identify three unvalidated assumptions: the recognition domain does not yet exist, ligand surface density on activated microglia is unmeasured, and shed soluble tumor necrosis factor alpha is predicted to act as a competitive inhibitor of receptor activation. A computational analysis of simulated resting-state electroencephalography, in which 45 of 171 electrode pairs differed after false discovery rate correction, is presented as a fully specified analysis workflow for delta-band connectivity as a secondary outcome measure rather than as evidence of effect, and yields effect sizes indicating that a rodent study would need roughly 11 animals per group. A four-arm validation plan is specified that separates the contribution of conditional regulation from that of genomic integration.

papers.title: Refractory Multivessel Coronary Artery Spasm Unresponsive to Renal Sympathetic Denervation, with Recurrent Transient ST-Segment Elevation and an Episode of Accelerated Idioventricular Rhythm: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Multivessel coronary artery spasm (CAS) is an uncommon, high-risk form of vasospastic angina that can produce transient ST-segment elevation mimicking acute myocardial infarction. Evidence to guide management when calcium channel blockers and nitrates fail is scarce, and renal sympathetic denervation (RSD) has been reported in very few patients; Case Presentation: A 53-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and dyslipidemia presented with nocturnal chest pain and inferior ST-segment elevation. Coronary angiography showed severe spontaneous spasm of the right coronary and left anterior descending arteries that resolved completely with intracoronary nitrate; the coronary arteries were otherwise angiographically normal. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I remained below 10 ng/L (reference 0-34 ng/L), and echocardiography was normal, fulfilling the criteria for definite vasospastic angina without myocardial infarction. The same two-vessel spasm was documented at a second angiogram three months later. Despite maximally tolerated dual calcium channel blockade, nitrates, and statin therapy, he required more than ten further admissions. A self-terminating accelerated idioventricular rhythm lasting about two minutes was recorded. No syncope or malignant arrhythmia occurred, and an electrophysiology review found no current indication for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. Radiofrequency RSD was performed off-label for refractory symptoms without complications, but at six months, his symptoms and admissions were unchanged; Conclusions: Our case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic difficulties in refractory CAS. Accelerated idioventricular rhythm after relief of spasm is a reperfusion rhythm and does not by itself indicate device therapy. In this patient, RSD did not control refractory multivessel CAS, a negative observation that adds to the very limited evidence on autonomic modulation in this setting.
